content.label: Not much to do without paying
All the App seems to do is yell at me for overreaching. And not in a gentle way.

I’m always the person to start going 110%, burn myself out, and stop working out for like a month because of it. I absolutely love this app because it’s finally gotten me back into regularly working out, at a healthy pace, and I feel incredible because I’m not burning myself out anymore. On top of the fact that the app’s features work wonders, it’s incredibly polished- every little button and slider feels great to use- every little thing seems like there was so much attention to detail put into it. The little flashes of colors, the incredible graphs, the little haptics that play when you slide a bar, everything is easy and fun to do. Massive kudos to the design team, from a designer myself.

I have written 3 emails to the company and there is 0 support. I even emailed Katrina who is the Co founder of the company regarding my concerns and I am simply not hearing back. So it seems there is no support at all.
The app is good, it’s just that everything is premium and it’s so expensive.

title.label: Good, but doesn’t consider health app workouts

content.label: The free version is pretty good. My only issue is that, when I forget to wear my apple watch and then manually track it on the health app, it doesn’t really get counted. And so the suggestions for how often I should be exercising are less accurate. Which is a tad annoying, but otherwise fine.

The algorithm they’re using to determine if you’re on track or need to rest is very, very basic. Like I think it’s only looking at duration of the activities I log manually and assuming I’m pushing myself to the limit.  It was telling me I need to go do something, so I logged the 3 hours of “daily chores” I did earlier in the day cleaning out the garage, which was in heart rate zone zero and I marked as just a little exertion. And then it said I was waaay overreaching! 

Whether it’s working as designed or not, I’m not learning much from this app about my fitness level and if I’m actually improving anything. It isn’t any more motivational than a plain old daily reminder.

I like the concept here, however I’ve noticed that the GPS while working out is having accuracy issues. While walking, it will go long distances without updating my location. I don’t have this problem when using the default workout app on my watch. What gives?

Issue has only gotten worse. The app is not very smart. I walk 3-4 times a week for 90 min and it keeps showing that I'm "over-reaching". My heart rate is normal, yet the app has not learned this routine. I have contacted support several times over the last few months, but no update has directly addressed this. Please fix.

Update: There is something wrong with the app. The last few days I have only walked for 30 min and it says I am "over reaching". I usually work out for 90 min and have no problems. Very interesting app. Really like the way it tracks and shows your health information 👍🏻 The reason for the three stars are the widgets. Not only do I find them a bit basic and lacking variety, but they don't update in the background. You have to click on the widget itself or open the app so the widget displays your current progress.

Overall, this app is fantastic. I use it exclusively on my Apple Watch. I have a request, though — and I think this is an opportunity Apple missed: I’d like to be able to cancel or abort a workout. 

I’m a homebody, and use Gentler Streak to track my morning household chores. But there are occasions where I’ve failed to stop the tracker. The next thing I know, another half hour has passed and I notice the tracker is still running. In those cases, a simple cancel button— perhaps beneath the “Done” one, and coupled with a “Do you really want to cancel?”  prompt — could stop the workout BEFORE it writes to the health data? I would much rather lose the 15 minutes of actual activity than keep a 45 minute instance I knew was false — I’d rather close the ring honestly and not have workouts later in the day affected by the mistake. 

Thank you so much!

I’ve been enjoying the encouragement notifications the app gives me after my workouts but today I’m running late and what do I see? A notification saying “ EXERCISE REMINDER You're about to wave adios to your streak. Start a Go Gentler workout and get back in the game.”  

Not ok. I don’t know about other people but my willpower works on POSITIVE reinforcement, not negative. Not wanting to feel like a loser is not a motivation for me. Sometimes I need a day off for very good reasons. Telling me I’m about to say “adios” to my streak makes me want to skip a day just to spite you. 

Reminders like “You got this!” and “You’re doing great, don’t stop!” are what will keep me going. This app is so good otherwise and the negativity just seemed surprising. I hope they can update the app to either ditch the negative reinforcement or give us a choice.
This is the worst workout app ever! I never get reminders to be active or suggestions on how to to be active. It’s the more worthless, passive app ever! Don’t waste your money on this!

title.label: Not impressed, poor quality nutrition info

content.label: It’s ok. It doesn’t give me a ton of unique information or metrics. I can get any information on the app from other free apps or basic programs for phone/watch. I’m an advanced practice registered dietitian and find the nutrition advice to be of poor quality, not science/evidenced based, outdated, and/or plain wrong. Just not impressed and kind of annoyed that this kind of low quality nutrition advice is prevalent and promoted.

I’ve downloaded and paid for the app to test it but I’m really disappointed in the app although it was recommended by Apple. Sorry, but this app is useless. I’m doing a normal walk with my dog and this app tells me I’m overreaching. lol seriously?! I’m happy and healthy person and I love my walks but I’m definitely not overreacting. Sad. I’ve deleted the app.

I paid for this app based on, Apple’s recommendation. If I take a little walk it tells me I’m overreaching for days. I’m so disappointed. This app encourages me to be a couch potato. No thanks by.  Given all my   life circumstances, I thought it would help. Don’t waste your money.

This is a good app , it doesn’t have a lot of functionality but it good for what it does. I am grossed out by the artwork they use - like the drawing of what looks like a bloody tampon for an article about working out with a period. Most of the drawings of an exercising heart are really ugly as well. If the got some more attractive or normal graphics it would be so much better

title.label: Must go premium to do anything

content.label: I was curious about this app and excited to see what it can do. Unfortunately you cannot see exactly what it can do without “going premium.” The price isn’t awful, but I don’t think I would use it enough to warrant the price.

The developers have made an app for which there’s zero way to even learn about the functions of the app without buying a subscription. There’s also no trial premium offered. That wouldn’t be an issue if the “basic” version of the app was functional but instead if you don’t immediately sign up for a year EVERY SINGLE ITEM YOU CAN TAP ON THE HOMEPAGE LOADS THE SAME SUBSCRIPTION SCREEN. There is literally no way to try out this app because of developer greed. There’s also no way to opt out of data collection or to have the profile you created delete. Bad practices from bad people.
Worthless! Overhyped! Does nothing

I am loving this app so far! I am still in the process of learning the ins and outs but I really love that it caters to your real life and understands that sick days, rest days and just taking time off happens.

title.label: Great way to stay fit but not burn out

content.label: It’s a great app to keep you moving, but to help you avoid burnout. The only thing I wished it could do is to see your past Activity Path points. You can only see 10 days back, but I wish I could see all of it.

title.label: Nifty for fitness, but harmful for womens health info

content.label:
Long story short: The fitness tracking seems good, but the womens health articles read like they’re written by a quack and shame contraceptive use for cramps. 

The app has seemed good so far, and I find it refreshing that they focus on not just active days, but rest days as well. It could be nice to be able to dig in a little deeper at times to understand how they come to their recommendations for you. I reeeaally don’t like their Womens Health articles, though. They frame menstrual cramps as if they’re the woman’s fault from being too stressed or having a poor diet. Yes, those things can contribute, but menstrual cramping is incredibly common and not just some behavioral issue that would be fixed if we all lived a little healthier. They also state that if you use contraceptives to for these issues, that you should “keep in mind they don’t really solve hormonal imbalances; they just clog up the symptoms”. One common cause of menstrual cramping is endometriosis. Endometriosis can be managed and prevented from progressing through the use of hormonal contraceptives. It doesn’t just “clog up the symptoms”. It’s a legitimate treatment for many health issues, and the alternative is other hormone treatment or surgery, which is far more invasive. Their description is not just misleading but almost like they’re shaming people who use contraceptives (or anything “synthetic”). This could easily be harmful to someone who doesn’t know much about the topic.

I have only been using the app for a couple of weeks, but I am feeling really optimistic about it. As somebody who has over exercised and even injured myself in the past, I like that this app tells you when you are over doing it. It also suggests alternatives including active recovery or simply taking a rest day. The activity path also adds an extra layer of motivation because I want to see it trend upward. I also really liked that the app was able to pick up my existing activity data and show me a summary of 2022. Thanks for creating such a wonderful app!

As well designed as this app is, the actually functionality of the app only sometimes works. Most of the time when loading the app I get a loading spinner that never goes away. If the app does load, workouts I’ve made don’t show up even though everything is set up correctly and synced with Apple Health. This app has great potential but these are huge bugs that make the app useless until they’re fixed.

title.label: A very nice app and concept! But…

content.label:
The app’s concept is lovely! However, if you are a seasoned athlete or advanced fitness fanatic, this is probably not the app for you. As an advanced athlete myself, I find the app constantly thinks I am “overreaching” the healthy progress zone. Normal training for me seems to be overtraining according the activity bar. 

I do enjoy the insights, which is mainly my purpose for using it at this point haha. But this is definitely an app geared more toward those in the beginning and intermediate stages of their fitness journey!

title.label: Great app, would love more insights

content.label: First, this app has been great in my habit building and motivation to just get up! I would love to see more items in the Insights section. I feel like I quickly went through everything and now there’s not much content to explore.

title.label: Very pleasant interface. Possibly too gentle?

content.label:
I just downloaded the app, and I REALLY enjoy the aesthetic of this application. It is very fun to interact with and I’m excited to check back in to see how it interprets my data.

I understand this app might be tailored to individuals who are just beginning their wellness/fitness/etc. journeys, but is there a way to raise the “overreaching” limit? Or possibly make the message more supportive? As soon as I plugged in my information Yorhart told me I was overreaching, when actually I’m feeling pretty enthusiastic about my training and life in general right now.

Or maybe the “overreaching” limit doesn’t need to be raised. But users are presented with goal options, and based on what goals we select Yorhart will support us differently?

- “Recovering from an injury? You might be overreaching.”

- “Hey there! Remember if your goal is to balance your personal and professional life, you may be slightly overreaching for your goal.”

- Or, “Hey go getter! Congratulations on exceeding your goal once again! Keep up the hard work and you’ll be setting a new goal before you know it!”

I hope any of this was worth while, and doesn’t sound too critical. I really enjoy the app, and even though it is literally called “Gentler Streak” I would just love to see a more supportive message when I’m feeling like a go getter. There’s so much potential here. And I will definitely keep using and sharing!

Thank you!

This seems like a seriously useful app. It's really got the right idea and the app really seems polished and clean without bugs. Great job on that. 

After using it for a week I notice it says I'm overreaching when I'm definitely not. I feel better than before. And I believe that's due to a couple reasons. It doesn't take into account sleep and it also doesn't take into account untracked activity. One of the missing ingredients here that make this app difficult to trust is that it doesn't tap into the Apple Watches ability to track other metrics in the background. Say I walk 15k steps that day in a bit of an abnormal day (this wasn't intentional exercise and I didn't track it) gentler streak has no idea and is still urging me to hit my target. The inverse is also true, if I have a lot of untracked activity history, gentler streak isn't accounting for that so it's really setting the bar low and telling me I'm constantly over reaching when really, I'm not. 
It also doesn't account for sleep which can also be tracked by a variety of devices and then pulled from apple health. I may sleep really great and be fully recovered but it makes no impact on how much I can do the next day. 

I would also like to know with a little more clarity if I follow the path, will I actually start to increase my fitness? Or will the path always peak me under what I'm capable of? Right now as it's constantly "overreaching" I feel a bit stifled. I know that's the point, but the problem is it tells me I'm pushing hard when I'm definitely not. I would like to feel like I'm actually overreaching when it says it.

I even bought the premium service. It’s not a very serious app for working out. Has a few graphics but is really nothing. I won’t recognize this. Btw I am a marathoner and workout 7 days a week it’s a utterly useless app that goes to peddle other apps

title.label: Finally a workout tracker that makes sense

content.label: I’ve been using this app for about a month now and I absolutely love it. I don’t feel pushed to workout when my body is worn out. It lets me know when I need to step it up or if what I’m doing will maintain my current fitness level. It also tells me when I absolutely need a rest or I’ll hurt myself. It’s simple to use and understand. This is the motivation and guidance I’ve been needing. I have been consistent in my work outs since downloading this app and I feel better about actually working out. I highly recommend trying this app.

title.label: Outdoor workouts do not record map/route?

content.label:
I just tried recording an outdoor walk with this app and it doesn’t seem to record the route walked! I’m surprised. Is this expected or a bug?

Update: it looks like the map route is recorded but only shows up in Gentler Streak app. It doesn’t show up in the Health app. Is there a way to get that map to show up in Health app?

This app is so delightful, and it’s so great seeing that they are still working on adding features regularly. I only wish there was more to go through! I open this app every day and the calories burned to food emoji comparison is soooo fantastic and the activity recaps are truly brilliant! 

Wondering if maybe under activities for the week overview there was a way to see the emojis of food burned for that week so far. Without having to go into each individual activity. Keep the updates coming!
What’s up with every app being a subscription. Jeeze - check the time on your phone for $49 a month… so over it.

I like that it’s not are relentless as apples ring system. Allows you to see if you are over or under training. I also really like that it suggests different workouts for you and shows you the intensity each would be so you can train at the right level to what you’re needs are
Wish there was an option for Pilates reformer.

I really like the idea of having rest days built into your streaks, but the execution in this app is just generally not great. There is almost no real data to look at, and if you do want to look at longer term trends it’s buried away in a non-intuitive manner. For example, you can’t scroll past the current week on the main view. 

I like the graph view of my activity compared to prior days (instead of rings) but I didn’t find it worth the subscription (or buying the app outright, which I do appreciate the option for!!)

I love the timer in the corner. I wish I could make it alert me in intervals. I like to set a timer between sets(I’m distracted easily) and have it buzz when times up so I don’t have to switch between apps.
I have just started using this app, but it seems to be in tune with my thinking. Logarithms are the key

First off, I’m writing this on my iPad cause it’s lots easier than hunt-peck on the iPhone. I’m surprised to find the app on the iPad, nonetheless, opening it I discovered I’d have to go thru the same initial setup routine I did on the iPhone. Yet, without doing it, the app informed me I’d already subscribed. So why wasn’t all my data there as well? The app itself is far superior to Apple’s own. Unlike theirs, this one is more realistic. For example, taking time off, including daily chores in one’s workout routines. I’m still unsure subscribing is necessary, nonetheless, I’m going thru with it because I believe in supporting those who have gone to the trouble to put such a fine app together. I also commend the developers for tying in Apples exercise data. It takes awhile to download it into the app, but there it all is. Improvements such as enlarging the timer on each exercise routine. For some reason, heart rate is the app’s #1 priority while exercising. Its there in BIG numbers while the timer is stuck in the top left corner in tiny figures. Swimming & not being able to clearly see the elapsed time makes things difficult. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a better exercise app than Apples.

Added Aug 24. Unfortunately, I’ve had to down rate this app due to it’s swimming choices. I did receive a reply regarding the timer, but her advice is wrong. Instead of moving the timer to the middle screen, it starts a separate timer altogether. When finished, swiping to the left to stop takes quite some time cause the watch doesn’t like wet fingers. Then, like EVERY exercise routine in Gentler, it takes a VERY HARD press to get the Done screen to appear. Why so much effort??? But the most egregious error is its failure to call up Apples water eject feature wherein we must spin the crown until hearing an audible sound informing us the watch is unlocked. I’ve no idea if water remains or not.  No matter what I do, that eject water feature just does not appear.

I read a lot about this app and was excited to try it, but during every day of the free trial it told me I was overworked and to take a rest day. Every day! The fact that I’ve had only rest days for a year kind of scares me — what body metrics is this thing reading and what is wrong with me?? Well, you can’t find out on the app or the website what inputs it’s using to tell you to rest. If it’s just a calibration problem that would be good transparency to put somewhere in the insights. Otherwise this company is simply withholding information rather than stopping me from being overwhelmed by it.

title.label: Suggestion and Review: Gentler Streak App

content.label: I have recently started using your app and became immediately attached to it! As a D1 athlete, I use my Apple Watch almost every day when it comes to seeing the number of calories I burnt, the distance I traveled, my average pace, and now my recovery meter! I wanted to make a recommendation for one of the activities on the app: Outdoor Rowing. Currently, the watch face only displays my calories burnt, the amount of time that has gone by, and my average heart rate. I would really like it if there was a way to customize it and see my distance as I row. Some additional features such as my pace, or stroke rate would be a great add-on as well. Overall, I'm super satisfied with the app that your team has created!
I’ve been using app for a month and I like it so far
I have been using this app for a while and I love it, works great and have several workouts other apps don’t have.

There are little articles that are not specific to my data- this can be found anywhere. Not sure how this is any better than apple health. It does not import nutritional info from other apps or apple health

I am unable to find the new activities as I am an avid Gardener and cannot see that with the update and list of activities?  I only see golf and gymnastics under the G’s and I’ve updated my phone and watch. Otherwise would give 5stars.

title.label: Helpful to learn to listen to body cues

content.label:
Updated: I’m blown away by how quickly my concerns about the food emojis being triggering were addressed in the app. I’m now a subscriber and have updated my rating. Thanks for being so open and responsive!

Old:
Why have a little emoji implying I burned off a slice of pizza during yoga? You seem to get with the whole concept of the app that people need a more supportive way to meet fitness goals, and the food icons just reek of diet culture. Really enough of a turn-off that I uninstalled the app.

I’ve been using Gentler Streak Premium for about a month, and it’s been a game changer for both my physical fitness and mental health. I now no longer feel guilty for taking a rest day, in fact now I embrace it! Counterintuitively, my cardio fitness (as measured by my VO2 max) and my strength have improved despite taking more days off. I now realize that I was likely doing too much activity and not resting enough. I’m working hard to stay in the green, although I still “overreach” about once a week. So far, I have nothing but good things to say about this app!

This app’s design does a beautiful job of actually motivating me to be active. You can exercise a little bit every day or a lot every couple days and the app will recognize it as keeping a streak as long as you do enough but not too much. I’ve always felt like the apple watch’s default metric view was too aggressive and doesn’t seem to have any way to really say “hey you’re pushing too hard.” It also has a way to easily compare your activity over different periods of time and set goals for yourself. Very much worth the $20/y

I got gentler streak as I thought it would better help me track my fitness and be more understandable than other apps like Aptive 
It tells me my body is struggling and I should take a few days off. 
So I do. 

Then it tells me my fitness is in decline and I need to work out. 
So I do…. 

Halfway through a workout the app is telling me I need to take a break because my body is struggling 🤯

Please make up your mind. 
I’ve been pushing myself at this level of 6 months and have no problem with it. So why does the app think I have a problem?

I’m not one of those elite athletes Apple seems to make their exercise apps for. This app scales the encouragement back to suit my exercise life perfectly. Otherwise it works just like the built-in watch workout app, so it can easily take its place. Highly recommended. Qq
